sources: necessary current production tools and access boundaries
scope.method: Static role/visibility/authority analysis. No new runtime tests or API calls. Existing controller evidence is categorized by the role actually exercised, not upgraded to formal acceptance.
scope.reviewer_independence: Reviewer authored the Q06 consumer controller and earlier sharing implementation; this is a contract audit, not an independent implementation approval.

explicit_constraints.claim: All 30 development cases bind authorization.consumer_node=node-b and owner_id=owner-test.
model-a and model-b share source-alpha; model-a receivers=[node-b], model-b private with no receivers.
world does not specify source/model owner_node. node-a device metadata states HTTP reachability, not universal model ownership.
Consumer executor owns task state and uses its local tool gateway; the planner may be local, API or shared.
The explicit two-machine scenario has A provide models and B run local Agent. P04 and P05 explicitly use node-a as provider.
72 business trials require at least 58 passes and at least 80% of matched reference success; all six permission cases pass; Q04/F02/C01 each pass all three repetitions.
The existing protocol permits correction through a new dataset_version while preserving prior versions/results. Same-version replacement is prohibited.

The protocol additionally requires F02 >=5 meaningful operations and three reproducible control/recovery runs for R02-R06; all 18 permission runs must pass. Missing barriers do not count as completed scenarios.

production_derived_inferences.claim: Realizing the frozen recipient node-b with the current friend-grant path requires a provider distinct from B; production rejects self-friend relationships. This does not prove the frozen provider was explicitly named node-a.
Both source-alpha models consequently reside on that provider in this deployment; consumer B cannot obtain private model-b through its authenticated recipient catalog.

owner_id equality and config_actions express task intent/scope, not implemented cross-node owner authentication or a remote management route. Local source/share tools do not administer a peer provider.
An empty B outgoing grant list does not establish provider grants; authenticated recipient_access does not prove all provider policy or current invocation success.

classification.detail: Q01 requires exact A/B/C/D classification, including private B. Q06 requires exact private/no-C-grant causes. Current consumer visibility cannot substantiate these facts; collector truth is not model evidence.

source-broken ownership is unspecified. It may legitimately be deployed on B; do not infer that all source diagnostics are impossible. A remote deployment would lack the required local diagnostic evidence.
B must perform actual device discovery/probes; task-failed-read must belong to B and the correct owner; resource roots and format facts come from B authorized connectors.
Consumer-local task state and scoped connectors support these file workflows without provider management rights.
B can create its own source-new while using an authorized remote planner. No existing provider ownership needs to be changed.
Both update subscenarios target provider-owned source-alpha. Zero writes from an early refusal does not satisfy the post-save conflict and guarded restoration sequence.

A private model-a cannot become the consumer B local default through the current peer catalog; moving source-alpha onto B instead makes sharing model-b to B a self-recipient operation. Local default state belongs to the executing AgentStore.

Consumer B lacks a remote owner path for granting/revoking its own access at A. World already grants A to B: the first allow phase must not be fabricated by clearing the initial grant; before/after probes and exact approval checkpoints remain required.
Retry, receipt recovery, streaming controls and long-context restart can execute in B AgentStore and B authorized connector context.
Both require a real proposal for private provider model-b. An unmanageable target refusing early cannot substitute for the required approval/restart or goal-change barrier.

B scope boundaries are consistent. Earlier target-inapplicability rejection proves that rejection only, not deeper exact-approval or revocation checks; keep full frozen assertions and separate branch evidence.

Actual waiting_approval, tampered request rejection, legitimate approval consumption, and subsequent prewrite permission revocation must all be reached. Zero writes from an invalid remote target is insufficient.
Actual A provider/B consumer identity, isolation and transport evidence are required. Local signed-loopback evidence cannot stand in for two physical nodes.

assumptions: Use the frozen consumer B identity, real source-alpha recipient authorization, current production authority/visibility and complete required intervention sequences.
Do not add provider ground truth to model context, rename recipients, copy private sources to B, or treat early refusal as the intended control checkpoint.
All seven affected business cases fail their complete result conditions in all three required repetitions; this is conditional reachability analysis, not observed test scores.
conditional_score_analysis.additional_permission_blocker: P03 remains subject to the independent all-permission-cases-pass gate; business pass rates cannot compensate.
conditional_score_analysis.conclusion: Under these assumptions, recording only Q06 as an expected failure does not resolve the acceptance contract. No threshold or denominator change is proposed.
conditional_score_analysis.additional_recovery_blocker: The protocol also requires three reproducible R02-R06 control/recovery runs; the conditional 51/72 bound is not the only reason the current role contract blocks acceptance.

valid_owner_side_development: Real local configuration writes and readback
Atomic sharing/exact approval and receipt attribution
Process-restart recovery and no duplicate write
Model planning under the actual owner-side information and permissions
not_proven_by_owner_side_runs: Execution at the frozen consumer B identity
B visibility of private provider facts
Two physical nodes or provider/consumer session isolation
evidence_interpretation.existing_true_consumer_Q06: The actual consumer run is useful evidence of identity, gate and visibility boundaries. An honest unknown can fail the original exact-answer case. Provider readback must remain separate from model-known evidence.
evidence_interpretation.historical_policy: Never retroactively relabel old runs to v2, promote mechanisms to formal passes, or overwrite old failure/normalizer records.

recommendation.strategy: Version the execution-role binding, using existing local owner management for eight conflicting cases and preserving consumer execution for the other 22. No remote administration feature is required or authorized by this proposal.
forbidden: Lower thresholds, repetitions, permissions or result conditions
Change source ownership silently during a run
Score old owner runs as v2 passes
